name: Mirion Technologies, Inc.

profile.description: Mirion Technologies, Inc. provides radiation detection, measurement, analysis and monitoring products and services for nuclear power, defense, laboratories and medical customers, operating Technologies and Medical segments. Recent acquisitions of Paragon and Certrec added nuclear safety-related components and regulatory software. Founder Thomas D. Logan has been CEO since 2005 and Chairman since February 2025; the company listed on the NYSE in 2021 through a merger with GS Acquisition Holdings Corp II.

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): Mirion has broadened from detection instruments into nuclear safety-related components and regulatory software via the Paragon and Certrec acquisitions, and it booked $49M of small modular reactor (SMR) orders in Q2 2026, up $42M year over year [1] — a significant new revenue stream, though acquired rather than built. AI Deployment (1/2): In February 2026 Mirion named its first Chief Artificial Intelligence & Digital Officer [3], and Logan says AI is compressing software development cycles [4], but no savings or AI products are quantified. Market Share (1/2): Mirion is an established player in radiation monitoring, but no share data was found. Pipeline (1/2): Backlog of more than $1.1B and SMR orders give visibility [1], but specific next-generation product launches with dates were not found. R&D Intensity (0/1): R&D of $38.9M is 4.2% of FY2025 revenue [5], low for an instrumentation company.

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): Mirion's focus on the safe use of ionizing radiation across nuclear power, defense and medicine is clear and purposeful, but no statement was found that is distinctive or proven as the competitive advantage. Community Impact (0/2): No foundation or quantified community investment was found; the company published its first Corporate Social Responsibility Report only in 2023 [7]. Employee Retention (0/2): No retention or tenure data was found. Insider Buying (0/2): No net open-market insider buying in the trailing 12 months was found; Logan's long tenure as founder-CEO since 2005 [3] is noted but is not buying evidence.

infrastructure.label: DEVELOPING
infrastructure.analysis: Calculated mechanically on 7 metrics (Growth sleeve, 10 weight units). D/E 67.7% (1.00) and TTM revenue growth 24.5% (1.00, mostly acquisition-driven; 2026 organic guidance is 5–7%) [1][6]. Revenue CAGR is 8.5% (0.90, 2x), computed over the four years FY2021 $668.3M to FY2025 $925.4M because FMP's FY2020 figure is the pre-merger SPAC shell with no revenue [5]. Forward P/E 27.8 (0.80). Profitability is weak: ROE 1.6% (0.11, 2x) and profit margin 2.7% (0.13), and FMP's forward PEG of 14.5 (0.00, 2x) reflects thin GAAP earnings [6][8]. Weighted sum 4.96/10 → 5. Liquidity: ~4.09M shares/day × $18.37 ≈ $75M/day, above the floor.

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (8/9): Mirion builds physical radiation detectors, dosimeters and safety-related nuclear components sold into heavily regulated nuclear, defense and medical settings — work AI cannot substitute. AI-driven data-center power demand supports the nuclear build-out that underpins its record backlog and SMR orders [1]. No analyst commentary found frames AI as a substitution risk. AI Opportunity (0/1): AI is being embedded in product development and operations under a new Chief AI & Digital Officer [3][4], but no AI revenue is quantified.

infinite_game.summary: Mirion has a real cause — making the use of radiation safe — and founder continuity under Logan since 2005 [3]. Sinek would be cautious, though: growth has come largely through serial acquisitions and a debt-heavy SPAC listing, headline 2026 growth of 22–24% is mostly acquired and FX versus 5–7% organic [1], and the culture is largely undocumented. Positioned for a long nuclear cycle, but it has not yet shown the purpose-driven consistency of an infinite player.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): Protecting people from ionizing radiation in power plants, hospitals and on the battlefield is service-oriented and enduring, and Logan has pursued it for two decades [3]. It has not been visibly tested by a costly choice, and investor communication centers on backlog and EBITDA margin [1].

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Mirion committed to nuclear and SMR capability before the current power-demand cycle and is investing to gain an 'early-adopter advantage' in AI [4]. The heavy reliance on acquisitions (Paragon, Certrec) [1] and the leveraged SPAC structure are more finite-game financial engineering.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): The founder has led since 2005, and the February 2026 executive appointments were framed as adding market focus rather than reacting to a crisis [3]. No employee-sentiment, tenure or turnover data was found, so this is scored as adequate.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): Mirion has extended from detection instruments into medical radiation QA, nuclear safety components and regulatory software [1][2] — adjacent expansions, not a fundamental reinvention.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): No management commentary was found acknowledging competitors' strengths or framing rivals as a source of improvement.

investment_thesis: Mirion is a direct play on a nuclear renaissance driven partly by AI data-center power demand. Q2 2026 revenue rose 19.7% to $266.8M, backlog exceeded $1.1B (up nearly 40%, legacy backlog +17%), and SMR orders reached $49M in the quarter [1]. Management reaffirmed FY2026 revenue of $1,129–1,147M, adjusted EBITDA margin of 25–26%, and adjusted free cash flow of $155–175M [1]. Goldman Sachs keeps a Buy rating with a $23 target [2].
thesis_continued: The bear case is quality of growth and valuation. Organic growth is guided at only 5–7%, with the rest from acquisitions and FX [1], and the full year depends on a second half guided to 7.5–11.2% organic growth [1]. GAAP profitability is thin — 2.7% net margin, 1.6% ROE, P/E of 167 — with $1.24B of debt [8]. Medical-segment order cancellations required a guidance mix shift, and the stock fell ~9% after Q2 results despite reaffirmed guidance [2].
key_catalysts: Execution on H2 2026 guidance of $605–623M revenue with 7.5–11.2% organic growth [1]
Conversion of $1.1B+ backlog and further SMR orders ($49M in Q2 2026) as new reactor programs advance [1]
Integration synergies from Paragon and Certrec in nuclear safety components and regulatory software [1]
Deleveraging from $155–175M adjusted free cash flow guidance [1]
key_risks: Organic growth of only 5–7% masked by acquisitions and FX [1]
Back-half-loaded guidance creates execution risk; shares fell ~9% after Q2 [2]
Thin GAAP earnings (2.7% margin) and $1.24B debt with modest interest coverage [6][8]
SMR and new-build nuclear timelines slipping on licensing or financing delays, deferring orders

backlog.note: Backlog exceeded $1.1B at Q2 2026, nearly 40% higher year over year (legacy backlog ex-Paragon/Certrec +17%), with $49M of SMR orders in the quarter. TTM book-to-bill is not disclosed. About 4.1 quarters of TTM revenue ($1.08B) [1].
